name: Muzammil Qazi
headline: Azure Data Engineer · AI Workflow Automation
introduction: I work with Azure data pipelines, data quality, and AI-assisted workflows to make everyday engineering and operations easier to understand and maintain.
about: I'm Muzammil, an Azure data engineer based in Pune. My experience at Cognizant connects enterprise operations with data engineering: understanding what a workflow needs to do, investigating where it breaks, and making the next handoff clearer.

My work spans ingestion with Azure Data Factory, transformations with Databricks and PySpark, and SQL-based validation and reconciliation. I'm especially interested in the practical layer around a pipeline: useful telemetry, understandable errors, and documentation people can actually use.

I'm applying AI to that same set of problems through diagnostic assistants, metadata-driven SQL generation, and retrieval over operational documents. My direction is simple: reliable data foundations, with automation that helps people make better decisions.

projects.title: From pipeline errors to a clearer next step.
projects.name: AI Data Pipeline Support Assistant
projects.summary: An assistant that interprets ADF execution traces and turns technical errors into diagnostic guidance and incident communication.
projects.problem: Pipeline failures leave engineers with execution traces, exceptions, and a time-sensitive investigation. Turning that information into a useful next step and a clear stakeholder update can involve repetitive work.
projects.contribution: Developed a troubleshooting utility to interpret Azure Data Factory execution traces and pipeline exceptions, produce diagnostic guidance, and draft validation SQL and incident communication.
projects.implementation: The résumé describes a Python and Streamlit utility using an LLM workflow with ADF error information and SQL validation context. Its outputs include likely failure context, troubleshooting steps, and structured communication.
projects.outcome: The documented result is a reusable diagnostic workflow that brings investigation and communication into one utility. No independently verified time savings or production deployment evidence is available, so no numerical performance claim is made here.
projects.boundary: Diagnostic guidance and generated SQL require engineering review. The available project description does not document the model provider, hosting environment, evaluation dataset, or measured accuracy.
projects.discussion: A useful next evidence step is a sanitized failure example, the assistant's response, and a record of which suggested checks were correct.

projects.title: Make the gaps in your data visible.
projects.name: Intelligent Data Quality & Reconciliation Framework
projects.summary: Reusable source-to-target checks that translate metadata into SQL validation, schema comparisons, and quality summaries.
projects.problem: Source and target datasets can disagree in schema, record counts, or expected values. Rewriting similar verification queries for each dataset makes quality reviews repetitive and harder to standardize.
projects.contribution: Designed a metadata-driven validation framework that generates source-to-target verification queries, compares schemas, runs reconciliation checks, and summarizes detected exceptions.
projects.implementation: Python and SQL support reusable checks driven by source and target metadata. The documented outputs include validation status, schema inconsistencies, reconciliation results, and unexpected record gaps.
projects.outcome: The project description supports a repeatable approach to validation and structured quality reporting. No public benchmark, coverage measurement, or verified reduction in review effort is available.
projects.boundary: Metadata quality and the chosen rules determine what a check can detect. The available material does not specify database permissions, deployment architecture, automated test coverage, or a production release.
projects.discussion: The most useful evidence would be a synthetic source/target pair, generated checks, expected discrepancies, and reproducible results.

projects.title: Put operational knowledge within reach.
projects.name: Enterprise Operations Knowledge Assistant
projects.summary: A RAG proof of concept for finding workflow instructions and troubleshooting guidance inside SOPs and runbooks.
projects.problem: Operational guidance often sits across process documents and runbooks. Finding the relevant instruction during an investigation can mean manually searching several sources.
projects.contribution: Built a proof-of-concept assistant using retrieval-augmented generation to retrieve contextual guidance from SOPs, runbooks, and internal-style operational documentation.
projects.implementation: The documented approach uses RAG and LlamaIndex to connect natural-language questions with relevant operational content. The use cases include workflow instructions, troubleshooting procedures, and escalation guidance.
projects.outcome: This is documented as an exploration of knowledge retrieval, prompt optimization, and contextual responses. It is not presented as a deployed enterprise assistant or as evidence of measured answer accuracy.
projects.boundary: The source material does not identify an embedding model, vector store, chunking configuration, evaluation results, or access-control implementation. No private operational documents are exposed on this website.
projects.discussion: A future public demonstration should use synthetic documents and measure grounded answers, retrieval relevance, and appropriate abstention.
